Indeed, all known applications of product-expanding codes in quantum error correction crucially rely on productexpansion for the codes along with their duals [19]–[22], in order to ensure good distance in both the X and Z bases. The only previously known collections of t > 2 such productexpanding codes were uniformly random codes over large alphabets, as shown in the recent work of [23]. Such higherorder (with t = 4) product-expansion was a crucial ingredient in the recent construction of nearly good quantum locally testable codes [22]. Theorem 7 may therefore mark progress towards constructing quantum locally testable codes with more algebraic structure, which has been proposed as a useful ingredient towards making such codes asymptotically good [39] or support transversal gates [11]. Though note that as described in Section V, in order to be directly applicable to the construction of [22], Theorem 7 would need to be extended to allow all t codes to be of the dual type. B. Proof Techniques Our proof of Theorem 7 builds upon the framework of maximally extendable (ME) codes introduced by [23], which in turn is closely related to the classical literature on maximally recoverable (MR) codes (see e.g. [40]). This framework studies codes that have “maximal,” or optimal, properties among all codes in a given family. For instance, given a family of classical codes, a MR code for the family is a code that can correct every pattern of erasures that is correctable by any code in the family. MR codes are typically characterized by having an appropriate set of minors of the generator or parity-check matrix be nonzero. Such codes can then often be constructed by sampling random codes from the family over sufficiently large fields, where the desired minors vanish with high probability by the SchwartzZippel lemma. [23] showed how to apply related ideas to prove higherorder product-expansion for uniformly random codes over large fields. Specifically, [23] first proved that an arbitrary number t of classical locally testable codes have productexpansion. Such codes necessarily have dual codes of low distance, which as mentioned above, precludes the desired quantum applications. However, [23] instead defined the notion of maximally extendable (ME) codes, which can be thought of as a version of MR for product-expansion. More concretely, [23] characterized the product-expansion of codes C1 , . . . , Ct as being equivalent (up to constant factors) to having certain minors be nonzero for the generator matrix of the dual tensor code C (1) +· · ·+C (t) (defined in Section II-B). Then because there exist (locally testable) product-expanding codes, these minors will generically be nonzero, meaning that they will be nonzero for uniformly random codes over sufficiently large alphabets by Schwartz-Zippel.
